key_insight: Wind shear and veer do not just change the incoming wind speed and direction; they also alter rotor induction, and together these geometric and inductive effects can cut actuator-disk power coefficient by more than 20%.
engineering_relevance: Accurate wind turbine power prediction in the atmospheric boundary layer should account for shear, veer, and wall-proximity effects because standard engineering models miss meaningful losses from changed rotor aerodynamics.
method: Concurrent-precursor LES of an actuator disk turbine in stratified atmospheric boundary layer conditions
Controlled inflow LES with shear and veer varied independently to isolate their contributions
Decomposition of performance changes into geometric rotor-equivalent wind speed effects and inductive aerodynamic effects
evidence_signal: The abstract reports LES results showing statistically significant efficiency reductions, with shear and veer together reducing power efficiency by more than 20% and earlier field campaigns observing losses above 15%.
watch_item: The results are based on actuator-disk LES and simplified inflow controls, so transferring the quantified losses directly to full-scale, blade-resolved turbines or all site conditions should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Influence of wind shear and veer on power, thrust, and induction of an actuator disk
